sentences.text:
Heard Sri Vijay Kumar Asthana, the learned counsel for the applicant as well as Sri Jayant Singh ,
the learned Additional Government Advocate-I appearing on behalf of the State and perused the
records.

2. The instant application has been filed by the applicant seeking anticipatory bail in F.I.R. bearing
Case Crime No. 53/2019, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 504, 506 Ipc, Police Station
Bhinga, District Shrawasti.

3. The aforesaid case has been registered on the basis of an F.I.R. lodged on 11.02.2019 against the
applicant, his father and brother, stating that some property dispute is going on between the
informant and the applicant's father and for this reason, the accused persons had beaten up the
informant at about 10:00 am on 25.08.2018 and had forcibly taken possession of the disputed land.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the affidavit filed in support of the application it has been contended that the applicant is innocent, he has falsely been implicated in the present case and that he has no criminal history.
5.

The applicant's brother-co-accused Rakesh has been granted anticipatory bail by means of an order dated 20.09.2023 passed by this Court in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application No.
2039 of 2023.

entities.text:
Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application No.
2039 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 6. The learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail but he could not dispute the aforesaid aspects of the matter.

7. Having considered the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and without making any observations which may affect the outcome of the case, I am of the view that the applicant is also entitled to be granted anticipatory bail on the ground of parity.
8. In view of the above, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.

Order Date :- 19.10.2023 Pradeep/-
